title: developer-cost-lab-product-brief-2026-02-08
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Overview
========

This product brief describes the Developer Cost Lab: a low-friction, sandboxed environment that bundles a simulated consumption runner, telemetry bridge to Redwood Console, and a lightweight cost-feedback SDK for developer workflows. The Lab is targeted at developer and platform teams who need safe, repeatable experiments to understand unit economics (tokens/embedding/throughput) for different model variants, batching and caching settings, and fidelity policies before committing to Dedicated or Private deployments.

Goals
-----

- Give engineers a fast feedback loop for cost-latency-quality tradeoffs without consuming production credits.
- Surface actional recommendations (batch sizes, kv cache policies, quantization profiles) through Redwood Optimize suggestions.
- Make simulated traffic reproducible and shareable across teams with seeded scenarios and named experiments.
- Integrate telemetry into Redwood Console so that cost signals tie back to the exact sandbox config and prompt set.

Scope and out-of-scope
----------------------

In-scope:
- Playbook and product UX for launching sandbox experiments from the Console and CLI.
- A sandbox runner that can emulate streaming and transactional workloads.
- SDK hooks to capture per-request fidelity toggles and synthetic token counts.
- Integration with Optimize to produce cost-saving recommendations.

Out-of-scope:
- Running full Dedicated GPU fleets for the lab (we use capacity-sliced emulator pools and local inference stubs).
- Persistent production-grade billing: sandbox runs consume dedicated credit buckets and do not affect customer invoices.

Why this product
-----------------

Teams frequently under- or over-provision when moving from prototyping to production because they lack reproducible cost-to-performance data. This leads to churn (migrating from Hosted to Dedicated prematurely), poor SLO choices, and surprises during contract negotiations. The Developer Cost Lab reduces risk by making tradeoffs visible and repeatable during onboarding and feature design.

User personas
------------

- Developer (individual contributor): wants a one-click way to simulate N=1000 chat sessions and get a per-utterance cost breakdown.
- ML Engineer / Platform: needs to compare quantization profiles across candidate models and capture quality regression metrics.
- Solutions Engineer / Sales: uses named experiments to demonstrate expected cost at target QPS for a prospective customer.

Key capabilities (high level)
----------------------------

1) Scenario Runner
- Seeded traffic generator supporting: conversational sessions, stateless generation, embeddings batches, and reranking workloads.
- Configurable arrival patterns: constant, poisson, burst (burst profile: amplitude, duration, recurrence).
- Output: synthetic traces formatted for Redwood Console ingestion (span IDs, route, model_variant, synthetic_token_counts).

2) Telemetry Bridge
- Lightweight agent that maps sandbox experiment metadata into Console schemas. Events emitted: experiment.start, run.metrics, experiment.snapshot.
- Cost inference: uses the same per-token unit economics engine as production but applies sandbox credit multipliers (configurable).

3) Developer Cost SDK
- Client-side hooks (Node/Python/Go) for: tagging prompt templates, annotating fidelity toggles, and marking golden prompts for quality capture.
- Local CLI to run sample scenarios and upload results for sharing.

4) Optimize integration
- Automatic recommendations for: batching policy (suggested batch sizes), kv cache prefixing, and quantization profile selection.
- Recommendations include estimated monthly delta (USD) and percentile latency impact.

Minimal success metrics (first 90 days)
---------------------------------------

- 100 distinct experiments created by internal developer teams.
- Average time-to-insight (experiment creation -> cost recommendation) < 10 minutes.
- At least 2 customer pilots convert to Dedicated trials with documented cost regressions prevented.

Requirements (PRD-style)
-------------------------

Functional requirements:
1. FR-1: Experiment lifecycle API (create/list/describe/stop) with immutable experiment snapshot export.
2. FR-2: Scenario DSL that can express: session length distribution, user message length distribution, and multi-stage reranking pipelines.
3. FR-3: Telemetry events must be queryable in Console with filters: experiment_id, model_variant, route, and timestamp range.
4. FR-4: Cost estimator must accept overrides for unit costs (quantized variant price, reserved capacity price) to model Dedicated pricing.
5. FR-5: SDK must capture 'fidelity_tag' semantics and allow developers to opt-in prompt capture for quality regressions.

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR-1: Experiment replay determinism: repeated runs of the same seeded scenario must produce token counts within +/- 3% across runs for the same model configuration.
- NFR-2: Telemetry latency: events from sandbox runner should appear in Console within 60s for 95% of events.
- NFR-3: Sandbox isolation: experiments must only consume from sandbox credits and not affect production quotas.

Design highlights
-----------------

Experiment DSL (example snippet)
- The DSL is YAML-like; example below (shown as plain text):

  scenario_name: small-chat-burst
  workload: conversational
  seeds: 42
  arrival_profile:
    type: burst
    amplitude: 200
    duration_seconds: 30
    recurrence_minutes: 10
  message_length_distribution:
    mean: 42
    p95: 120
  model_variants:
    - name: redwood-ft-lite-q4
      quant_profile: q4_0
    - name: redwood-moderate
      quant_profile: q8_1

Telemetry & Console mapping
- Events emitted include structured fields: experiment_id, run_id, scenario_name, model_variant, batch_size, cache_hit_rate, synthetic_token_count, latency_ms. These are mapped to Console columns for per-experiment dashboards.

Recommendation engine contract
- Input: experiment snapshot + observed metrics. Output: ranked suggestions each with: id, description, expected_cost_delta_percent, expected_p50_latency_delta_ms, confidence_score (0-1).

Pricing/packaging notes
-----------------------

- Sandbox consumption is billed to internal credits. For external pilots we offer a hosted sandbox add-on priced as a monthly seat per-engineer + simulated-credit bucket. Suggested pilot package (beta):
  - 10 seats, 100k simulated tokens/day, priority onboarding support.

- Recommendations must include two price-model projections: Hosted per-token baseline and Dedicated reserved capacity equivalent. This is required for sales/SE playbooks to justify transition decisions.

Roadmap and milestones
----------------------

Q1 2026 (alpha)
- Deliver core scenario runner and local SDKs. Basic Console ingestion for experiment metadata.

Q2 2026 (beta)
- Add Optimize recommendation hook and richer scenario DSL. Implement pilot billing paths and pilot SE playbook.

Q3 2026 (GA)
- Multi-model comparison reports, Dedicated pricing projection support, and per-experiment sharing links in Console.

Rollout steps and runbook excerpt
---------------------------------

1) Internal alpha: enable feature flag for dev and platform teams. Collect feedback (2 weeks).
2) Beta pilot: invite 3 customers (SE-led) to run guided experiments; capture conversion feedback.
3) GA: open to self-serve; surface in onboarding checklist.

Runbook checklist for pilot SEs:
- Verify sandbox credit buckets (billing admin).
- Preload recommended prompt sets and golden prompts.
- Confirm Console experiment dashboard shows run metrics within 60s.
- Run a 1-hour burst scenario and validate cost projection divergence between q4 and q8 variants.

Appendices
----------

A. Example Console query (pseudo-SQL)
  SELECT experiment_id, model_variant, SUM(synthetic_token_count) as tokens, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p50_latency
  FROM telemetry.events WHERE experiment_id = '<id>' AND timestamp BETWEEN '<start>' AND '<end>' GROUP BY experiment_id, model_variant

B. Suggested experiment naming conventions
- team-feature-scenario-date (e.g., payments-ocr-batch-20260312)

C. Security note
- Sandbox runner will not accept customer data marked as PHI/PII for hosted pilots. All prompt captures must be redacted or flagged and stored with restricted confidentiality.
